summary: No critical vulnerabilities. Two findings worth addressing: error messages may leak implementation details about the signing service, and the DB error fallthrough in sign.ts could silently bypass idempotency in degraded mode.

findings.title: Error message from adapter.sign() leaks internal details to MCP callers
findings.description: When adapter.sign() throws, the raw error message is returned to the MCP caller: `'Mnemonik signing failed — service may be unavailable. Details: ${msg}'`. If the SDK throws with JWT contents or internal URL structures in the message, this reaches the client. The SDK's redactJWT() is applied to SDK error messages already, but third-party network errors (e.g. from fetch) may not be redacted.
findings.recommendation: Apply redactJWT() (from @mnemonik-xyz/sdk errors.ts) to `msg` before embedding in the returned error string. Import `redactJWT` from '@mnemonik-xyz/sdk' and use `redactJWT(msg)` in the error template.

findings.title: DB query failure silently falls through to re-sign — idempotency bypass under degraded DB
findings.description: If the memory_attestations table SELECT fails (e.g. DB connection error), sign.ts logs a warning and falls through to sign again. This means a DB blip causes double-signing of the same content. In participate mode (Arweave+Solana), double-signing creates two on-chain records with user cost implications.
findings.recommendation: In participate mode (when mode='participate' is detectable), propagate the DB error rather than silently falling through. Add an optional `mode` field to SignMemoryInput or detect participate mode from the adapter. For local mode, fallthrough is acceptable (no cost). This is medium-priority — the current behaviour is still correct for local mode and safe for cloud (just creates a duplicate sign).
findings.note: The mode is private to MnemonikAdapter so detecting it from sign.ts requires interface extension. Deferring to Task 5/task lead decision.

findings.title: Error from adapter.verify() leaks internal details
findings.description: Same pattern as SA-1: `err.message` from verify() is embedded in the returned error string. The SDK redacts JWTs in its own errors but network-level errors from fetch() do not go through redactJWT.
findings.recommendation: Apply redactJWT(msg) before embedding in error strings — same fix as SA-1.

findings.title: createMnemonikAdapter warning log includes error details that may contain credential hints
findings.description: Line 134: `Details: ${msg}` in the stderr warning. The msg comes from MnemonikAdapter constructor which calls parseJwtPayload() — parseJwtPayload may include JWT segments in its error message. The SDK's redactJWT is applied in MnemonicError.constructor but parseJwtPayload error format may differ.
findings.recommendation: Apply redactJWT(msg) to the Details fragment in the startup warning string.
findings.note: parseJwtPayload errors are descriptive strings without raw JWT content (e.g. 'jwt: missing sub claim'), so risk is low. Apply redactJWT as defence-in-depth.
